## Radial face moments and the face-centroid shift {#sec-ch03-facemoments}

The flux through an $x_2$ or $x_3$ face is a face average, weighted by the face's own area measure. On a Cartesian
grid that weight is uniform in $x_1$; on the spherical-polar and cubed-sphere grids an $x_2$/$x_3$ face spans
$r\,\mathrm{d}r$ times an angular factor while the cell spans $r^2\,\mathrm{d}r$ times one. Two numbers follow from
the face measure: its $x_1$ variance, which sets the size of the covariance of two fields over the face, and the
offset between where a cell average lives and where the face average lives. Both enter the $O(\Delta x_1^2)$
face-flux corrections of @sec-ch04-fluxcov. This scheme supplies them exactly; the flux use is in @sec-ch04-fluxcov.

Local symbols: $x^{\mathrm{A}}_{1,i}$ the $x_1$ centroid of an $x_2$ or $x_3$ face of cell $i$
on the face's own measure [$\mathrm{m}$]; $\mathtt{face\_moment2\_x1}_i$ the second central moment of $x_1$ on that measure
[$\mathrm{m^2}$] and $\mathtt{face\_centroid\_shift\_x1}_i = x_{1,i} - x^{\mathrm{A}}_{1,i}$ the face-centroid shift [$\mathrm{m}$],
written with the code's names because they live on the face measure, not the cell measure of $\sigma_i^2$[^rg-fb5c884bea4a] and
$\delta_i$[^rg-3aec6aa6f14d]; $I_n$ the integral $\int_{r_-}^{r_+} r^n\,\mathrm{d}r$ [$\mathrm{m}^{n+1}$].

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** The exact $x_1$ second moment of an $x_2$/$x_3$ face and the exact offset between a cell's volume centroid
and that face's centroid, in cancellation-free form (@eq-ch03-facemoments-moment, @eq-ch03-facemoments-shift), plus a
per-type flag that the shift is identically zero.

**Data.** In: radial faces $r_\pm$ [m]. Out: `face_moment2_x1` [m$^2$] and `face_centroid_shift_x1` [m] per cell,
on the face's own area measure, distinct from the cell measure of $\sigma_i^2$ and $\delta_i$.

**Placement.** Read by the face-flux covariance in each stage's $x_2$/$x_3$ flux; `face_moment2_x1` is evaluated once per block and kept until `x1f` is replaced or modified or the device or dtype changes.

**Activation.** Read by `SNAP_FLUX_COVARIANCE` (@sec-ch12-flux-covariance), on unless set to
`0`/`false`/`off`/`no` or empty (any case); the helpers exist on every grid.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact, not truncated; zero shift on Cartesian.

**Evidence.** `test_radial_face_moments`, `test_coordinate`; checks `[C1]` to `[C3]` (sympy, exact); the ctest
entries were not run for this chapter at the pin (missing evidence).
:::

On the Cartesian grid the shift is zero by construction, and a host constant of the coordinate type,
`face_centroid_shift_zero`, says so, so the covariance can skip its centroid parts without reading the device. A
test keeps the flag equal to the shift for every coordinate type.

### Derivation

The derivation is in {{< code docs/derivations/289-covariance-x3-curved.md >}}
§2.7 (the moment) and §2A.1 (the two centroids); it is rewritten here in the report's notation. The angular factor
of an $x_2$/$x_3$ face does not vary along $x_1$ on one face, so it cancels in every average and the face weight is
$w(r) = r$. With $\Delta x_1 = \Delta x_{1,i}$ and $x^{\mathrm{m}} = x^{\mathrm{m}}_{1,i} = \tfrac12(r_- + r_+)$, so that
$r_\pm = x^{\mathrm m} \pm \Delta x_1/2$, the three integrals are

$$
\begin{aligned}
I_1 &= \tfrac12\left(r_+^2 - r_-^2\right) = x^{\mathrm m}\Delta x_1, \\
I_2 &= \tfrac13\left(r_+^3 - r_-^3\right) = \Delta x_1\left((x^{\mathrm m})^2 + \frac{\Delta x_1^2}{12}\right), \\
I_3 &= \tfrac14\left(r_+^4 - r_-^4\right) = \Delta x_1\,x^{\mathrm m}\left((x^{\mathrm m})^2 + \frac{\Delta x_1^2}{4}\right),
\end{aligned}
$$

and the two centroids are their ratios:

$$
\begin{aligned}
x^{\mathrm{A}}_{1,i} &= \frac{I_2}{I_1} = \frac{12(x^{\mathrm{m}})^2 + \Delta x_1^2}{12\,x^{\mathrm{m}}}, \\
x_{1,i} &= \frac{I_3}{I_2} = \frac{3x^{\mathrm{m}}\left(4(x^{\mathrm{m}})^2 + \Delta x_1^2\right)}{12(x^{\mathrm{m}})^2 + \Delta x_1^2},
\end{aligned}
$$

the second being the spherical-polar volume centroid of @eq-ch03-sphpolar-centroids. The second central moment on the
face measure is $(I_3 - 2x^{\mathrm{A}}I_2 + (x^{\mathrm{A}})^2I_1)/I_1 = I_3/I_1 - (x^{\mathrm A}_{1,i})^2$, since
$x^{\mathrm A}_{1,i}I_1 = I_2$. With the integrals above,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{I_3}{I_1} - \left(x^{\mathrm A}_{1,i}\right)^2
&= (x^{\mathrm m})^2 + \frac{\Delta x_1^2}{4} - \frac{\left((x^{\mathrm m})^2 + \Delta x_1^2/12\right)^2}{(x^{\mathrm m})^2} \\
&= (x^{\mathrm m})^2 + \frac{\Delta x_1^2}{4} - (x^{\mathrm m})^2 - \frac{\Delta x_1^2}{6} - \frac{\Delta x_1^4}{144(x^{\mathrm m})^2}
 = \frac{\Delta x_1^2}{12} - \frac{\Delta x_1^4}{144(x^{\mathrm m})^2},
\end{aligned}
$$

that is,

$$
\mathtt{face\_moment2\_x1}_i = \frac{\Delta x_1^2}{12}\left(1 - \frac{\Delta x_1^2}{12(x^{\mathrm{m}})^2}\right).
$$ {#eq-ch03-facemoments-moment}

@eq-ch03-facemoments-moment is `radial_face_moment2_` ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::radial_face_moment2_ >}}). Subtracting the two
centroids directly would cancel, because both are close to $x^{\mathrm{m}}$. Doing the algebra first, over the common
denominator $12x^{\mathrm m}\left(12(x^{\mathrm m})^2 + \Delta x_1^2\right)$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
x_{1,i} - x^{\mathrm A}_{1,i}
&= \frac{36(x^{\mathrm m})^2\left(4(x^{\mathrm m})^2 + \Delta x_1^2\right) - \left(12(x^{\mathrm m})^2 + \Delta x_1^2\right)^2}
        {12x^{\mathrm m}\left(12(x^{\mathrm m})^2 + \Delta x_1^2\right)} \\
&= \frac{144(x^{\mathrm m})^4 + 36(x^{\mathrm m})^2\Delta x_1^2 - 144(x^{\mathrm m})^4 - 24(x^{\mathrm m})^2\Delta x_1^2 - \Delta x_1^4}
        {12x^{\mathrm m}\left(12(x^{\mathrm m})^2 + \Delta x_1^2\right)},
\end{aligned}
$$

which gives the exact

$$
\mathtt{face\_centroid\_shift\_x1}_i = \frac{\Delta x_1^2\left(12(x^{\mathrm{m}})^2 - \Delta x_1^2\right)}{12\,x^{\mathrm{m}}\left(12(x^{\mathrm{m}})^2 + \Delta x_1^2\right)}
= \frac{\Delta x_1^2}{12\,x^{\mathrm{m}}} + O\!\left(\frac{\Delta x_1^4}{(x^{\mathrm{m}})^3}\right).
$$ {#eq-ch03-facemoments-shift}

@eq-ch03-facemoments-shift is `radial_face_centroid_shift_` ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::radial_face_centroid_shift_ >}}). On a Cartesian grid
the two measures are the same uniform weight, so the moment is $\Delta x_1^2/12$ and the shift is zero; these are the base-class
values `face_moment2_x1` and `face_centroid_shift_x1` ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::face_centroid_shift_x1 >}}, {{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::face_moment2_x1 >}}). Both formulas are exact,
not truncated; @eq-ch03-facemoments-moment recovers $\Delta x_1^2/12$ as $\Delta x_1/x^{\mathrm{m}}\to0$.

::: {.callout-important title="Check"}
The centroids, the moment and the shift are checked against the exact integrals in sympy (`[C1]` to `[C3]`).[^fm-c]

### Numerical method

Both helpers return one value per $x_1$ cell, ghosts included, shaped like `dx1f`, from the face array alone. A face
with $x^{\mathrm{m}}\le \Delta x_1/2$ (an $x_1$ ghost that reaches $r\le0$) is degenerate: the moment's curvature correction
and the shift are set to zero there, and the divisors are clamped to $10^{-300}$ so the masked branch never divides by
zero. Spherical-polar and gnomonic grids override the virtual methods to call the radial forms; on the gnomonic grid
the cell volume is the same $r^2$ integral times the solid angle (@sec-ch03-gnomonic), so the same shift applies even
though its `x1v` is the midpoint. They are evaluated when the covariance correction asks for them, in the stage, before
the $x_2$/$x_3$ fluxes. @fig-ch03-facemoments-ratio plots both against $\Delta x_1/x^{\mathrm{m}}$.

*The zero-shift flag.* On the base measure `face_centroid_shift_x1` returns `zeros_like(dx1f)` unconditionally
({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::face_centroid_shift_x1 >}}), so every centroid part of the covariance
is an exact zero. The covariance therefore asks a second virtual, `face_centroid_shift_zero`
({{< code src/coord/coordinate.hpp CoordinateImpl::face_centroid_shift_zero >}}), and skips those parts when it is true.
It is a literal of the coordinate type, not a test of tensor contents: `true` in the base class, so Cartesian
inherits it; `false` in `SphericalPolarImpl`
({{< code src/coord/spherical_polar.hpp SphericalPolarImpl::face_centroid_shift_zero >}}) and `GnomonicEquiangleImpl`
({{< code src/coord/gnomonic_equiangle.hpp GnomonicEquiangleImpl::face_centroid_shift_zero >}}), the two classes that
override the shift; and `false` in `CylindricalImpl`
({{< code src/coord/coordinate.hpp CylindricalImpl::face_centroid_shift_zero >}}). Cylindrical builds no `dx1f`, so the
base shift has nothing to take `zeros_like` of, and its faces are $r$-weighted, so its shift is not zero in general.
The flag is read in three places: the `centroid` parts of `_flux_covariance`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::_flux_covariance >}}), the same in `scalar_flux_covariance`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::scalar_flux_covariance >}}), and the shifted pressure of the geometric
source in `HydroImpl::forward` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}). Because the flag comes from
the type, it holds no state that a re-mesh or `.to()` could leave stale. Whether skipping the centroid parts changes
any bit of a Cartesian run is **not measured at the pin**: no committed check compares the two paths.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch03-facemoments-ratio
#| fig-cap: "The radial face moment divided by its Cartesian value $\\Delta x_1^2/12$ (solid) and the face-centroid shift divided by its leading term $\\Delta x_1^2/(12x^{\\mathrm{m}})$ (dashed), against the relative cell width $\\Delta x_1/x^{\\mathrm{m}}$. Both are dimensionless and tend to $1$ as the cell becomes thin; the moment is the Cartesian one to within $\\Delta x_1^2/(12(x^{\\mathrm{m}})^2)$."
#| fig-alt: "Two curves starting at 1 at zero relative width and bending down as the width grows."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch03.figures.fig_facemoments_ratio import make_fig
make_fig()
```

: Code map of the radial face moments. {#tbl-ch03-facemoments-code}

In step order (@tbl-ch03-facemoments-code):

1. The caller asks the coordinate for `face_moment2_x1` (only when its per-block copy, keyed on the `x1f` tensor,
   its version, the device and the dtype, is missing or stale) and `face_centroid_shift_x1`; virtual dispatch picks the
   grid's form ({{< code src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp SphericalPolarImpl::face_centroid_shift_x1 >}},
   {{< code src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp SphericalPolarImpl::face_moment2_x1 >}}).
2. `radial_face_moment2_` forms $\Delta x_1$ and $x^{\mathrm{m}}$ from the faces and masks the degenerate cells with
   `torch::where` ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::radial_face_moment2_ >}}).
3. `radial_face_centroid_shift_` evaluates the cancellation-free quotient and masks the same cells
   ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::radial_face_centroid_shift_ >}}).
4. The covariance reads `face_centroid_shift_zero` and skips its `centroid` parts when it is true
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::_flux_covariance >}}).

**How to use it.** There is no YAML key: the helpers exist on every grid and are read by the face-flux covariance,
which is on by default and off with an environment switch read once per run. From `build/bin`, with the
complete deck and driver built as described in the preface, run:

```bash
SNAP_FLUX_COVARIANCE=0 ./straka.release straka_single.yaml
```

`false`, `off`, `no` or the empty string (any case) also turn it off; anything else is on.
Nothing is refused; on Cartesian the zero-shift flag skips the centroid parts. The cancellation-free shift
@eq-ch03-facemoments-shift and its degenerate-face mask are
({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::radial_face_centroid_shift_ >}}):

```cpp
  auto h2 = h.square();
  auto twelve_r2 = 12. * rbar.square();
  auto shift = h2 * (twelve_r2 - h2) /
               (12. * rbar * (twelve_r2 + h2)).clamp_min(1.e-300);
  // degenerate face (an x1 ghost reaching r <= 0): no meaningful centroid
  return torch::where(rbar > 0.5 * h, shift, torch::zeros_like(h));
```

and the switch is ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::flux_covariance >}}):

```cpp
  static const bool on = [] {
    auto v = get_env("SNAP_FLUX_COVARIANCE", "1");
    std::transform(v.begin(), v.end(), v.begin(),
                   [](unsigned char c) { return std::tolower(c); });
    return !(v.empty() || v == "0" || v == "false" || v == "off" || v == "no");
  }();
```

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_radial_face_moments` | the hand rationals equal the integrals | $10^{-13}$ relative | double evaluation of the $I_n$ |
| `test_radial_face_moments` | the closed forms equal the rationals | $10^{-14}$ relative | a few operations of round-off |
| `test_radial_face_moments` | per-cell indexing on a four-cell column | $10^{-14}$ abs., $10^{-12}$ rel. | as above, and the integrals' cancellation |
| `test_coordinate` | the zero-shift flag equals "the shift is all zero" for each coordinate type, in float64 and float32; cylindrical's flag is `false` | exact (boolean) | the test's `EXPECT_EQ` |

: Tests of the radial face moments. C++ entries carry the build suffix (`.release`). {#tbl-ch03-facemoments-tests}

The cases are the three `RadialFaceMoments` tests `the_rationals_are_the_integrals`,
`closed_forms_match_the_exact_integrals` and `one_value_per_cell_on_a_multi_cell_column` of
{{< code tests/test_radial_face_moments.cpp >}}; the cells $[1.5, 2.5]$, $[3, 5]$, $[1, 2]$ have shift $47/1176$, $47/588$, $13/252$ and moment $47/576$, $47/144$,
$13/162$, as listed in `kCells` ({{< code tests/test_radial_face_moments.cpp kCells >}}). The check reproduces these
rationals exactly (`[C2]`). The test runs on CPU, one process; the helpers are pure tensor functions with no
device-specific path. It was not run for this chapter at the pin (missing evidence).

The tripwire is the `Coordinate` test `face_centroid_shift_zero_matches_the_shift` of
{{< code tests/test_coordinate.cpp >}}, in the `test_coordinate` ctest. It builds a block of each coordinate type, cartesian, cylindrical, spherical-polar and
gnomonic-equiangle, in float64 and again after `.to(float32)`. For the three types that build a shift it requires
`face_centroid_shift_zero()` to be true exactly when `face_centroid_shift_x1()` is all zero, and the shift to have the
block's dtype; for cylindrical, which builds none, it requires the flag to be `false`. A new type that overrides the
shift without the flag fails it. That the test fails when a flag is forced to the wrong value is **not measured at
the pin**: no committed run records it.

### Limits

No known limits beyond the degenerate-face mask, which drops the curvature correction on ghost cells that reach
$r \le 0$, and one rule: the zero-shift flag is a host constant that nothing checks against the device at run time.
A coordinate type that overrides `face_centroid_shift_x1` must also return `false` from `face_centroid_shift_zero`, or
the covariance drops its centroid parts on that grid; only the tripwire test enforces this. The helpers are used only
by the face-flux covariance; their effect on the solution belongs to @sec-ch04-fluxcov. The switch combinations that
are tested are listed in the switch coverage matrix, @sec-ch12-matrix.
